sentences.text:
This appeal arises out of the award dated 05.07.2016 passed by 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bastar, place Jagdalpur (C.G.) in Claim Case No.134/2014 awarding compensation of Rs.7,34,400/- with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the appellant/claimant.
2.

entities.text: 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bastar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The claim of appellant/claimant before the Tribunal, in brief, was that on 16.03.2013, while appellant/claimant Mangalram Pandey along with her wife was going from Sonarpal to his village Mangalram Pandey vs Ramesh Singh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94904013/
1

on a motorcycle, respondent No.1 - Ramesh Singh driving the offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration No. CG 04 G 7545 rashly and negligently dashed his motorcycle from behind near village Joba, as a result of which, Mangalram suffered grievous injuries on his legs, knees, head and other parts of the body.
The claimant was given initial treatment at RNT Hospital Kondagaon, then he was shifted to Yashwant Hospital, Raipur for better treatment where he was admitted from 17.03.2013 to 30.03.2013.
His left leg was completely crushed, so his left leg had to be amputated from the knee due to which he became permanently disabled.
Upon report being made in this regard, crime was registered against respondent no.1 (Driver of the offending vehicle) at PS Kondagaon, District Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.
3. It was claimed that before the accident, he ran hotel and grocery shop from which he earned Rs.8,000/- per month.
On account of the accident, he received several grievous injuries and his left leg had to be amputated from knee, due to which he suffered 80% permanent disability.

Therefore,
the claimant preferred an application before the Claims Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.23,57,400/- for disability, loss in future income, physical and mental agony, medical expenses and also under other heads.
4. Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents brought on record, assessed the income of the decease at Rs.3000/- per month i.e. Rs.36,000/- per annum.

Since the claimant suffered 80% permanent disability due to the accident, loss of income was assessed at Rs.28,800/-
per annum.
Considering the age of the claimant to be 47 years, multiplier of 13 was applied and the total loss of income worked out to Rs.3,74,400/-.

In addition, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,85,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.1,00,000 for prosthetic leg, Rs.25,000 towards loss of income for 3 months, Transportation, Nutritious food and Attendant and Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.7,34,400/- in favour of the claimant with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of application till its realization.

Hence,
this appeal is for enhancement.

5. Learned counsel appearing for appellant/claimant submits that the Claims Tribunal has failed to consider the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant and awarded a total compensation of Rs.7,34,400/- which is a very small amount and needs to be enhanced.
He submits that the income of Appellant has been underestimated whereas his income was much higher than the amount determined by the Tribunal.

He next submits that t he Tribunal has erred in not considering future prospects while computing compensation as it failed to appreciate that the deceased would have earned much more if he had not met with the accident.

He submits that the left leg of appellant was amputated from the knee and the Tribunal has awarded only one lakh rupees for artificial leg whereas according to Dr. Surendra Shukla, the cost of getting artificial leg ranges from Rs.1,25,000 to 4,50,000.

He next submits that the amount given for pain and suffering is also minimal and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K. S. Muralidhar v. R.
Subbulakshmi and another reported in 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3385 it should be enhanced suitably.
Thus, prayed for modification of the impugned award enhancing the compensation suitably.
6.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. In a motor accident claim case, what is important is that, the compensation to be awarded by the Courts/Tribunals should be just and proper compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It should neither be a meager amount of compensation, nor a Bonanza.
9. Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
10. It is an injury case.

The claimant has brought on record his permanent disability certificate (Ex.
A-7) issued by District Medical Board, Maharani Hospital, Jagdalpur, Bastar (CG).
According to the said certificate, there was 80% of permanent disability due to amputation of left leg.
This fact also stands proved from the statement of Dr. L. L. Thakur who was a member of the Medical Board and had put his signature in the disability certificate.
Thus, from the evidence it is clear that due to the accident, the claimant sustained 80% permanent disability.
11. As per the claim of appellant/claimant Mangalram Pandey, he was earning Rs.8,000 by running hotel and grocery shop.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of appellant at Rs.3,000 per month as no documentary evidence has been produced regarding his income.
The incident occurred on 16.03.2013 and as per the notification by Labour Department, the minimum wages of even an unskilled labour at that point of time was Rs.4,646/-.
Hence, the income of the appellant is assessed at Rs.4,646/- per month i.e. Rs.55,752/- per annum.
12. The Tribunal has not considered future prospects while calculating compensation.

In the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, the future prospects would be 25% of the income and after adding future prospects of Rs.13,938, the amount comes to Rs.69,690.
13.

Taking into consideration the age of claimant to be 47 yeas at the time of accident and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier would be 13 and after applying the said multiplier, loss of income due to permanent disability amounts to Rs.7,24,776/-.
14.

sentences.text: The contention of the appellant is that since his left leg had to be amputated from the knee resulting in 80% permanent disability, he requires a prosthetic leg to function.
According to the appellant, the amount of Rs.1,00,000 awarded by the Tribunal for artificial limb is too less and needs to be enhanced.

Mangalram Pandey vs Ramesh Singh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94904013/
3 15.

In the case of Mohammad Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain v. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation passed in Civil Appeal No. 9070-9071 of 2022 dated 09/12/2022, the injured was found to have permanent disability in his right leg, where the Hon'ble Supreme Court, while expressing the concept of Just and Proper Compensation for prosthetic limb, passed an award of additional amount of Rs.12,80,000/- for the prosthetic limb and its maintenance, which reads as follows:
"22.

entities.text: Mohammad Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain v. Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court has awarded a compensation of Rs.5,20,000/- for the prosthetic limb and Rs.50,000/- towards repair and maintenance of the same.
The Appellant submits that the cost of the prosthetic limb itself is Rs. 2,60,000/- and the life of the prosthetic limb is only 5-6 years.
The prosthetic limb also requires repair and maintenance after every 6 months to 1 year, and each repair costs between Rs.15,000 to Rs.20,000/-.
This would mean that the prosthetic limb would last the Appellant for only 15 years under the current compensation.
The Appellant at the time of the accident was aged 37 years and has a full life ahead.

It has been clearly stated by this Court in the case of Anant Son of Sidheshwar Dukre (Supra) that the purpose of fair compensation is to restore the injured to the position he was in prior to the accident as best as possible.

The relevant paragraph of the judgment is being extracted herein:
"In cases of motor accidents leading to injuries and disablements, it is a well settled principle that a person must not only be compensated for his physical injury, but also for the non-pecuniary losses which he has suffered due to the injury.
The Claimant is entitled to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life and enjoy those things and amenities which he would have en- joyed, but for the injuries."
"The purpose of com- pensation under the Motor Vehicles Act is to fully and adequately restore the aggrieved to the position prior to the accident."

23. As per the current compensation given for the prosthetic limb and its maintenance, it would last the Appellant for only 15 years, even if we were to assume that the limb would not need to be replaced after a few years.
The Appellant was only 37 years at the time of the accident, and it would be reasonable to assume that he would live till he is 70 years old if not more.

We are of the opinion that the Appellant must be compen- sated so that he is able to purchase three prosthetic limbs in his lifetime and is able to maintain the same at least till he has reached 70 years of age.

For the Pros- thetic limbs alone, the Appellant is to be awarded com- pensation of Rs.7,80,000 and for maintenance of the same he is to be awarded an additional Rs.
5,00,000/-."

16. In the present case, injured-appellant Mangalram, whose age is considered to be 47 years at the time of the accident, has been found to have 80% permanent disability due to amputation of his left leg from the knee.
According to the statement of Dr. Surendra Shukla, the orthopedist of Yashwant Hospital, Raipur who treated the appellant, the cost of artificial leg ranges from Rs.1,25,000 to 4,50,000.
More than 12 years have passed since the accident took place.
At present, the cost of artificial leg must have increased.

Considering all these facts, it would be appropriate to award an Mangalram Pandey vs Ramesh Singh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94904013/
4 amount of Rs.5,00,000 for artificial leg.
17. As regards the amount awarded under pain and suffering, the appellant has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K. S. Muralidhar(supra).
In the said case, the injured had sustained 90% permanent disability and he was awarded 15,00,000 for pain and suffering.

However, in the said case no amount was awarded for artificial limb, the injured was employed as a workman in L.M. Glassfibre (India) Pvt. Ltd., his gross salary was Rs.28,221 per month and he sustained multiple fractures, such as a fracture of co-vertebra with anterior dislocation over C7, Cervical Spine revealed dislocation of C-6 over C-7, Bilateral transverse process fracture and C-6 fracture both laminae and body.
Therefore, on the ground of difference in facts, the judgment relied upon by the Insurance Company would not be applicable in the present case.
Hence, the amount of Rs.50,000 awarded by the Tribunal towards pain suffering seems to be proper.

18. In addition, the amount given towards loss of income for 3 months, transportation, special diet &
nutritious food and Attendant is enhanced from Rs.25,000 to Rs.40,000.
However, the amount of Rs.1,85,000 awarded towards medical expenses is found to be proper.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant would become entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,99,776/- in the following manner:-
 Heads Compensation Modified/enhanced  awarded by Tribunal Compensation  Loss of income due to 3,74,400 7,24,776  permanent disability  Medical expenses 1,85,000 1,85,000  Artificial leg & its 1,00,000 5,00,000  maintenance  Loss of income for 3 months 25,000 40,000  during treatment,
 Transportation, special diet  & nutritious food and  Attendant  Pain and suffering 50,000 50,000

Total compensation Rs. 14,99,776/-
19.

Thus, the total compensation is recomputed as Rs.14,99,776/- from which after deduction of Rs.7,34,400/- as awarded by the Tribunal, the enhanced compensation would be Rs.7,65,376/-.
20.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.7,65,376/- in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
Accordingly, the impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

Mangalram Pandey vs Ramesh Singh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94904013/
5 21.

The said communication be made in Hindi (Deonagri) language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimant resides.
